mainEntity.name: What is the Five Surfaces methodology?

acceptedAnswer.text: Five Surfaces is an adversarial risk framework for LLM-backed systems that maps five distinct attack surfaces: Input/Output (direct prompts, jailbreaks), Retrieval (RAG corpora, indirect injection), Tool-Call/MCP (function calling, server poisoning), Model (weights, training-data extraction), and Runtime (sandbox escape, agent loops). Each surface has distinct threat models and remediation patterns. Unlike traditional web-app pentesting, Five Surfaces is purpose-built for LLM security and covers the 69 risk classes most commonly found in production.

mainEntity.name: What is MCP and why do I need to audit it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Model Context Protocol (MCP) allows LLM agents to call external tools and services. Each MCP server is unsigned code with privileged access to your model's context window—effectively a supply-chain risk. Vectorbreak treats MCP as the critical attack surface it is. Our scanner detects tool impersonation, prompt-injection sinks, credential leakage, and unsafe configurations before they become production incidents.

mainEntity.name: How does Vectorbreak's red-teaming differ from traditional pentesting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traditional pentesting assumes attacker goals like data theft or system access. AI red-teaming assumes the attacker is trying to make the model say or do something the developer didn't authorize. The threat model is fundamentally different—it's about behavioral control, not system compromise. Vectorbreak's methodology focuses on model-specific vectors like prompt injection, jailbreaks, context confusion, and tool misuse that web-app methodologies miss entirely.
